subject: Chemistry
topic: Ideal Gas Laws and Gas Stoichiometry
subtopic: Boyle's, Charles's, Avogadro's Laws, PV = nRT & Dalton's Partial Pressures
text: MoEYS Grade 11 Chemistry Gas Unit: Ideal Gas Laws and Gas Stoichiometry (ច្បាប់ឧស្ម័នបរិសុទ្ធ និងស្តូគ្យូមេទ្រីឧស្ម័ន). Combines Boyle's Law (P_1 V_1 = P_2 V_2 at constant T), Charles's Law (V_1/T_1 = V_2/T_2 at constant P), Gay-Lussac's Law (P_1/T_1 = P_2/T_2 at constant V), and Avogadro's Law into the Combined Gas Law P_1 V_1 / T_1 = P_2 V_2 / T_2 and Ideal Gas Law PV = nRT (R = 0.0821 L atm/(mol K) or 8.314 J/(mol K)), plus gas density d = PM/(RT) and Dalton's Law of Partial Pressures P_total = sum P_i.

source.section: Boyle's, Charles's, Avogadro's Laws, PV = nRT & Dalton's Partial Pressures

metadata.topic_khmer: ច្បាប់ឧស្ម័នបរិសុទ្ធ និងស្តូគ្យូមេទ្រីឧស្ម័ន
metadata.subtopic_khmer: ច្បាប់បอย-ម៉ារីយ៉ូត ច្បាប់ឆាល ច្បាប់អាវ៉ូកាដ្រូ សមីការ PV = nRT និងសម្ពាធផ្នែក
metadata.khmer_description: សិក្សាច្បាប់ឧស្ម័ន (បอย-ម៉ារីយ៉ូត ឆាល ហ្គេ-លុយសាក់ អាវ៉ូកាដ្រូ) សមីការឧស្ម័នបរិសុទ្ធ PV = nRT ដង់ស៊ីតេឧស្ម័ន និងច្បាប់សម្ពាធផ្នែករបស់ដាល់តុន។
metadata.starter_problem: PV = nRT, \quad P = 2\text{ atm}, \; V = 11.2\text{ L}, \; T = 273.15\text{ K. Find moles } n.
learning_objectives: Apply Boyle's, Charles's, Combined, and Ideal Gas Laws with Kelvin temperature
Calculate molar mass M = mRT/(PV) and gas density d = PM/(RT)
Apply Dalton's Law of Partial Pressures P_i = X_i P_total to gas mixtures

concepts.title: Combined & Ideal Gas Laws (សមីការឧស្ម័នបរិសុទ្ធ PV = nRT)
concepts.summary: Relating P, V, n, and T at STP (0 deg C, 1 atm, V_m = 22.4 L/mol) and general conditions.
concepts.body: At STP (0 deg C = 273.15 K and 1 atm), 1 mol of any ideal gas occupies V_m = 22.4 L. At any P, V, T, PV = nRT = (m/M)RT, which rearranges to molar mass M = dRT/P.

concepts.title: Dalton's Law of Partial Pressures (ច្បាប់សម្ពាធផ្នែករបស់ដាល់តុន)
concepts.summary: Total pressure of non-reacting gases equals the sum of individual partial pressures.
concepts.body: In a mixture of gases, P_total = P_1 + P_2 + ... = (n_total R T)/V, and each component's partial pressure is P_i = (n_i / n_total) P_total = X_i P_total.

khmer_terms.Ideal Gas Laws and Gas Stoichiometry: ច្បាប់ឧស្ម័នបរិសុទ្ធ និងស្តូគ្យូមេទ្រីឧស្ម័ន
khmer_terms.Boyle's, Charles's, Avogadro's Laws, PV: ច្បាប់បอย-ម៉ារីយ៉ូត ច្បាប់ឆាល ច្បាប់អាវ៉ូកាដ្រូ សមីការ PV = nRT និងសម្ពាធផ្នែក
khmer_terms.ideal gas law: សមីការឧស្ម័នបរិសុទ្ធ
khmer_terms.Boyle's law: ច្បាប់បอย-ម៉ារីយ៉ូត
khmer_terms.molar volume: មាឌម៉ូលឧស្ម័ន V_m
khmer_terms.partial pressure: សម្ពាធផ្នែក
khmer_terms.mole fraction: ប្រភាគម៉ូល

prerequisites: Moles n = m/M and Kelvin temperature T = t + 273.15

formulas.name: Ideal Gas Law, Combined Gas Law & Gas Density
formulas.conditions: R = 0.082 L atm/(mol K) when P in atm and V in L

examples.problem: Find the number of moles of an ideal gas occupying V = 11.2 L at P = 2.0 atm and T = 273.15 K.

exercises.prompt: An unknown gas has density d = 1.96 g/L at STP (V_m = 22.4 L/mol). Find its molar mass M and identify the gas.
solution_steps: M = 1.96 g/L * 22.4 L/mol = 43.9 approx 44 g/mol (CO_2).
Step 1: Match the gas constant R to your pressure and volume units (R = 0.082 L atm/(mol K) or 8.314 J/(mol K)).
Step 2: Always convert Celsius to Kelvin: T = t + 273.15.

common_misconceptions.text: Using R = 8.314 when P is in atm and V is in liters.
common_misconceptions.correction: When P is in atm and V is in L, use R = 0.0821 L atm/(mol K); use R = 8.314 when P is in kPa and V is in L (or P in Pa and V in m^3).

subject: Chemistry
subtopic: Molar Concentration, Mass Percentage, Conversion & Dilution Law
text: MoEYS Grade 11 Chemistry Solutions Unit: Aqueous Solutions, Concentration and Dilution (សូលុយស្យុង កំហាប់ និងការពង្រាវ). Covers molarity C_M = n/V (mol/L), mass concentration C_m = m_solute / V (g/L), mass percentage C% = (m_solute / m_solution) * 100%, the conversion formula C_M = (10 * d * C%) / M (where d is solution density in g/mL), and conservation of solute moles during dilution: n_1 = n_2 => C_1 V_1 = C_2 V_2.

source.section: Molar Concentration, Mass Percentage, Conversion & Dilution Law

metadata.topic_khmer: សូលុយស្យុង កំហាប់ម៉ូល និងការពង្រាវ
metadata.subtopic_khmer: កំហាប់ជាម៉ូល កំហាប់ជាភាគរយ ទំនាក់ទំនង C% និង CM និងច្បាប់ពង្រាវ
metadata.khmer_description: គណនាកំហាប់ម៉ូល (CM) កំហាប់ជាភាគរយម៉ាស (C%) រូបមន្តទំនាក់ទំនង CM = 10·d·C%/M និងការពង្រាវ ឬលាយសូលុយស្យុង។
metadata.starter_problem: C_1 V_1 = C_2 V_2, \quad C_1 = 2.0\text{ M}, \; V_1 = 50\text{ mL}, \; V_2 = 250\text{ mL. Find } C_2.
learning_objectives: Calculate molarity C_M = n/V, mass percentage C%, and solute mass m = C_M V M
Convert between mass percentage C% and molarity C_M using solution density d
Solve dilution and solution-mixing problems using C_1 V_1 = C_2 V_2 and C_f = (C_1 V_1 + C_2 V_2)/(V_1 + V_2)

concepts.title: Molarity, Mass Percent & Density Conversion (កំហាប់ម៉ូល និងកំហាប់ភាគរយ)
concepts.summary: Linking C_M = n/V and C% = (m_ct / m_s) * 100% via C_M = 10 d C% / M.
concepts.body: For 1 L (1000 mL) of solution with density d (g/mL), solution mass is m_s = 1000d g, solute mass is m_ct = 10 d C% g, and molarity is C_M = 10 d C% / M.

concepts.title: Dilution & Mixing of Solutions (ការពង្រាវ និងការលាយសូលុយស្យុង)
concepts.summary: Conservation of solute moles during water addition: C_1 V_1 = C_2 V_2.
concepts.body: Adding pure water to a solution increases volume from V_1 to V_2 = V_1 + V_water without changing the moles of solute, so C_1 V_1 = C_2 V_2.

khmer_terms.Solutions, Molarity and Dilution: សូលុយស្យុង កំហាប់ម៉ូល និងការពង្រាវ
khmer_terms.Molar Concentration, Mass Percentage, Co: កំហាប់ជាម៉ូល កំហាប់ជាភាគរយ ទំនាក់ទំនង C% និង CM និងច្បាប់ពង្រាវ
khmer_terms.solution: សូលុយស្យុង
khmer_terms.molarity: កំហាប់ជាម៉ូល (CM)
khmer_terms.mass percentage: កំហាប់ជាភាគរយ (C%)
khmer_terms.dilution: ការពង្រាវសូលុយស្យុង

prerequisites: Molar mass M and solution volume conversion (1 L = 1000 mL)

formulas.name: Molarity, Mass Percent & Dilution Equations
formulas.expression: C_M = \frac{n}{V} = \frac{m}{MV}, \quad C\% = \frac{m_{\text{solute}}}{m_{\text{solution}}} \times 100\%, \quad C_M = \frac{10 \cdot d \cdot C\%}{M}, \quad C_1 V_1 = C_2 V_2

examples.problem: 50 mL of 2.0 M HCl is diluted with water to a final volume of 250 mL. Find the final molarity C_2 and the volume of water added.
solution_steps: Step 2: Volume of water added = V_2 - V_1 = 250 - 50 = 200 mL.

exercises.prompt: Find the molarity of commercial HCl solution with C% = 36.5% and density d = 1.18 g/mL (M_HCl = 36.5 g/mol).

solution_steps: Step 1: Convert mL to L when computing n = C_M * V.
Step 2: Use C_1 V_1 = C_2 V_2 for dilutions and n_total = n_1 + n_2 for mixing same-solute solutions.

common_misconceptions.text: Substituting V_water (volume added) instead of total final volume V_2 = V_1 + V_water in C_1 V_1 = C_2 V_2.
common_misconceptions.correction: V_2 in C_1 V_1 = C_2 V_2 is always the total final solution volume.

subject: Chemistry
text: MoEYS Grade 11 Chemistry Thermochemistry Unit: Reaction Enthalpy and Hess's Law (ទែម៉ូគីមី និងច្បាប់ហែស). Enthalpy change Delta H is negative for exothermic reactions (ប្រតិកម្មបញ្ចេញកម្ដៅ, Delta H < 0) and positive for endothermic reactions (ប្រតិកម្មស្រូបកម្ដៅ, Delta H > 0). By Hess's Law, the overall enthalpy change of a reaction depends only on initial and final states: Delta H^0_rxn = sum n Delta H^0_f(products) - sum m Delta H^0_f(reactants), or from bond energies: Delta H = sum E_bonds_broken - sum E_bonds_formed.

metadata.topic_khmer: ទែម៉ូគីមី និងច្បាប់ហែស
metadata.subtopic_khmer: អង់តាល់ពីនៃប្រតិកម្ម កាឡូរីម៉ែត្រ និងច្បាប់ហែស (Hess)
metadata.khmer_description: សិក្សាបម្រែបម្រួលអង់តាល់ពី (ΔH) នៃប្រតិកម្មបញ្ចេញកម្ដៅ និងស្រូបកម្ដៅ អង់តាល់ពីកកើតស្តង់ដា ច្បាប់ហែស និងថាមពលសម្ព័ន្ធគីមី។
learning_objectives: Classify reactions as exothermic (Delta H < 0) or endothermic (Delta H > 0) and calculate heat q = m c Delta T
Calculate reaction enthalpy Delta H^0_rxn using standard enthalpies of formation Delta H^0_f and Hess's Law cycles

concepts.title: Hess's Law & Standard Enthalpy of Formation (ច្បាប់ហែស និងអង់តាល់ពីកកើត)
concepts.summary: Products minus reactants for Delta H^0_f; broken minus formed for bond enthalpies.
concepts.body: The standard enthalpy of formation Delta H^0_f of any pure element in its standard state (O_2(g), H_2(g), C(graphite)) is 0 kJ/mol. When reversing a thermochemical equation, flip the sign of Delta H; when multiplying coefficients by k, multiply Delta H by k.

khmer_terms.Thermochemistry and Hess's Law: ទែម៉ូគីមី និងច្បាប់ហែស
khmer_terms.Exothermic/Endothermic Enthalpy, Calorim: អង់តាល់ពីនៃប្រតិកម្ម កាឡូរីម៉ែត្រ និងច្បាប់ហែស (Hess)
khmer_terms.enthalpy change: បម្រែបម្រួលអង់តាល់ពី ΔH
khmer_terms.standard enthalpy of formation: អង់តាល់ពីកកើតស្តង់ដា
khmer_terms.bond energy: ថាមពលសម្ព័ន្ធ

formulas.name: Hess's Law & Calorimetry Equations
formulas.expression: \Delta H^\circ_{\text{rxn}} = \sum n\Delta H^\circ_f(\text{products}) - \sum m\Delta H^\circ_f(\text{reactants}), \quad q = mc\Delta T

examples.problem: Calculate \Delta H^\circ_{\text{rxn}} for CH_4(g) + 2O_2(g) \to CO_2(g) + 2H_2O(l) given \Delta H^\circ_f(CH_4) = -75, \Delta H^\circ_f(CO_2) = -394, and \Delta H^\circ_f(H_2O) = -286\text{ kJ/mol}.
solution_steps: Step 1: Note Delta H^0_f(O_2) = 0 kJ/mol (element in standard state).
Step 2: Sum for products = (-394) + 2(-286) = -966 kJ.
Step 3: Delta H^0_rxn = -966 - (-75 + 0) = -891 kJ/mol.

exercises.prompt: How much heat is required to warm 200 g of water (c = 4.18 J/(g C)) from 25 deg C to 75 deg C?
hints: Use q = m c Delta T with Delta T = 50 C.

solution_steps: Step 1: Multiply each species' Delta H^0_f by its stoichiometric coefficient.
Step 2: Compute sum(products) - sum(reactants) carefully watching negative signs.

common_misconceptions.text: Using products minus reactants for bond energies instead of reactants (broken) minus products (formed).
common_misconceptions.correction: For formation enthalpies Delta H^0_f, use Products - Reactants; for bond energies, breaking bonds is endothermic (+) and forming bonds is exothermic (-), so use Broken - Formed.

subject: Chemistry
subtopic: Oxidation Numbers, Oxidizing/Reducing Agents & Half-Reaction Balancing
text: MoEYS Grade 11 Chemistry Redox Unit: Oxidation Numbers and Redox Balancing (ប្រតិកម្មអុកស៊ីតកម្ម-រេដុកម្ម). Oxidation is an increase in oxidation number (loss of e^-); reduction is a decrease in oxidation number (gain of e^-). The oxidizing agent (អុកស៊ីតករ) gains electrons and is reduced; the reducing agent (រេដុករ) loses electrons and is oxidized.

source.section: Oxidation Numbers, Oxidizing/Reducing Agents & Half-Reaction Balancing

metadata.topic_khmer: ប្រតិកម្មអុកស៊ីតកម្ម-រេដុកម្ម និងចំនួនអុកស៊ីតកម្ម
metadata.subtopic_khmer: ចំនួនអុកស៊ីតកម្ម អុកស៊ីតករ-រេដុករ និងការថ្លឹងសមីការរេដុក
metadata.khmer_description: កំណត់ចំនួនអុកស៊ីតកម្មនៃធាតុក្នុងសមាសធាតុ និងអ៊ីយ៉ុង សម្គាល់អុកស៊ីតករ និងរេដុករ ព្រមទាំងថ្លឹងសមីការអុកស៊ីតកម្ម-រេដុកម្មតាមកន្លះសមីការអេឡិចត្រុង។
metadata.starter_problem: \text{Find the oxidation number of Mn in } \text{KMnO}_4 \text{ and Cr in } \text{K}_2\text{Cr}_2\text{O}_7.
learning_objectives: Determine oxidation numbers of elements in neutral compounds and polyatomic ions
Identify the oxidized species, reduced species, oxidizing agent, and reducing agent
Balance redox reactions in acidic and neutral media using oxidation-number or half-reaction methods

concepts.title: Rules for Oxidation Numbers & Redox Agents (ចំនួនអុកស៊ីតកម្ម និងអុកស៊ីតករ-រេដុករ)
concepts.summary: Sum of oxidation numbers equals 0 in a neutral molecule and equals the ion charge in a polyatomic ion.
concepts.body: Pure elements have oxidation state 0; O is usually -2, H is +1, alkali metals are +1. In a redox reaction, total electrons lost by the reducing agent must equal total electrons gained by the oxidizing agent.

khmer_terms.Oxidation-Reduction Reactions and Oxidat: ប្រតិកម្មអុកស៊ីតកម្ម-រេដុកម្ម និងចំនួនអុកស៊ីតកម្ម
khmer_terms.Oxidation Numbers, Oxidizing/Reducing Ag: ចំនួនអុកស៊ីតកម្ម អុកស៊ីតករ-រេដុករ និងការថ្លឹងសមីការរេដុក
khmer_terms.oxidation number: ចំនួនអុកស៊ីតកម្ម (n.o)
khmer_terms.half-reaction: កន្លះសមីការអេឡិចត្រុង

formulas.name: Oxidation Number Conservation Rule
formulas.conditions: All chemical species and balanced redox equations

examples.problem: Find the oxidation number of Mn in KMnO_4 and Cr in Cr_2O_7^{2-}.

exercises.prompt: Balance the redox reaction: Cu + HNO_3(dilute) -> Cu(NO_3)_2 + NO + H_2O.
hints: Cu goes from 0 to +2 (loses 2e^-); N goes from +5 to +2 (gains 3e^-). Multiply Cu by 3 and NO by 2.
solution_steps: Combine with spectator NO_3^-: 3Cu + 8HNO_3 -> 3Cu(NO_3)_2 + 2NO + 4H_2O.
Step 1: Assign oxidation numbers to all atoms and identify which elements change state.
Step 2: Multiply oxidation and reduction half-reactions so electrons cancel.

common_misconceptions.text: Calling the substance that gets oxidized the oxidizing agent.
common_misconceptions.correction: The substance that gets oxidized (loses electrons) is the reducing agent (រេដុករ); the substance that gets reduced is the oxidizing agent (អុកស៊ីតករ).

topic: Organic Chemistry: Hydrocarbons (Alkanes, Alkenes, Alkynes & Benzene)
subtopic: Homologous Series, Isomerism, IUPAC Naming, Addition & Markovnikov's Rule
text: MoEYS Grade 11 Chemistry Organic Unit: Hydrocarbons (អ៊ីដ្រូកាបួ). Covers saturated alkanes C_n H_{2n+2} (single bonds, substitution & combustion), unsaturated alkenes C_n H_{2n} (C=C double bond, cis/trans geometric isomerism, electrophilic addition of H_2, X_2, HX, H_2O following Markovnikov's Rule, and polymerization), alkynes C_n H_{2n-2} (C#C triple bond), and aromatic hydrocarbons (benzene C_6H_6).

metadata.khmer_description: សិក្សាអ៊ីដ្រូកាបួឆ្អែត (អាល់កាន) និងមិនឆ្អែត (អាល់សែន អាល់ស៊ីន) ព្រមទាំងអ៊ីដ្រូកាបួអារ៉ូម៉ាទិច (បង់សែន)៖ រូបមន្តទូទៅ នាមវលី អ៊ីសូមែ ប្រតិកម្មជំនួស ប្រតិកម្មបូកតាមវិធានម៉ាកូវនីកូវ និងប្រតិកម្មចំហេះ។
learning_objectives: Identify homologous series formulas: alkanes C_n H_{2n+2}, alkenes C_n H_{2n}, alkynes C_n H_{2n-2}, and arenes C_n H_{2n-6}
Apply IUPAC nomenclature and predict major products of HX or H_2O addition to unsymmetrical alkenes using Markovnikov's Rule
Balance complete hydrocarbon combustion equations and determine molecular formulas from CO_2 and H_2O yields

concepts.title: Homologous Series & Combustion of Hydrocarbons (ស៊េរីអូម៉ូឡូក និងប្រតិកម្មចំហេះ)
concepts.summary: General formulas and complete combustion to CO_2 + H_2O.
concepts.body: Complete combustion of C_x H_y is C_x H_y + (x + y/4)O_2 -> x CO_2 + (y/2) H_2O. For alkanes, n(H_2O) > n(CO_2) with n(alkane) = n(H_2O) - n(CO_2); for monoalkenes, n(H_2O) = n(CO_2).

concepts.title: Addition Reactions & Markovnikov's Rule (ប្រតិកម្មបូក និងវិធានម៉ាកូវនីកូវ)
concepts.summary: In HX or H-OH addition to an unsymmetrical alkene, H bonds to the C=C carbon with more H atoms.
concepts.body: When H-X (HCl, HBr, H-OH) adds across an unsymmetrical double bond R-CH=CH_2, the hydrogen atom attaches to the doubly bonded carbon that already has more hydrogens (-CH_2), while X attaches to the more substituted carbon (-CH-), giving R-CHX-CH_3 as the major product.

examples.problem: Write the equation and IUPAC name of the major product formed when propene (CH_3-CH=CH_2) reacts with HBr.
solution_steps: Step 1: Propene CH_3-CH=CH_2 is an unsymmetrical alkene.
Step 2: By Markovnikov's Rule, H attaches to C-1 (-CH_2) and Br attaches to C-2 (-CH-).
Step 3: Major product is CH_3-CHBr-CH_3 (2-bromopropane).

exercises.prompt: Complete combustion of 0.10 mol of an alkene produces 0.40 mol of CO_2. Find the molecular formula of the alkene.
hints: Number of carbons n = n(CO_2) / n(alkene).

solution_steps: Step 1: Identify the longest continuous carbon chain containing the principal multiple bond.
Step 2: Number from the end nearest the double or triple bond.

common_misconceptions.text: Numbering an alkene chain to give substituents the lowest locants instead of giving the C=C double bond the lowest locant.
common_misconceptions.correction: The C=C double bond takes priority over alkyl or halo substituents when numbering the parent chain.
